question: Why must Bāhunandana refrain from killing the one granted protection?
premises: The speaker commands Bāhunandana not to kill.
The speaker has already granted fearlessness.
The granted protection binds the addressee's action.
inference: Bāhunandana must not kill because the speaker has given the target fearlessness.
plain_english: Do not kill, son of Bāhu; I have granted fearlessness.
